1\. Configured name breaks host routing 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness 
create_url_adapter now passes SERVER_NAME into Werkzeug even when host matching is enabled, so
route matching uses the configured host instead of the request's actual host. Host-specific routes
on any other request host incorrectly return 404.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description Passing configured `SERVER_NAME` to `bind_to_environ` while host matching is enabled binds the adapter to the configured host rather than the request host, causing valid host-specific routes to return 404. ## Issue Context Werkzeug host matching routes against the full host. Restore the host-matching guard so `server_name=None` is passed in that mode, and add coverage combining `host_matching=True`, a configured `SERVER_NAME`, and a route on a different request host. ## Fix Focus Areas - src/flask/app.py[438-450] - tests/test_basic.py[1460-1478] ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

2\. Disabled subdomains reject valid hosts 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness 
Using None for an empty default subdomain lets Werkzeug derive a subdomain from the request host
even though subdomain_matching is disabled. Ordinary routes therefore return 404 for alternate
hosts and configured subdomains, contradicting existing behavior and tests that expect 204.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description When subdomain matching is disabled and the map's default subdomain is empty, passing `None` causes Werkzeug to derive a subdomain from the request host and reject otherwise valid ordinary routes. ## Issue Context Pass an explicit empty string when `default_subdomain` is empty, preserving the distinction between an intentionally empty subdomain and Werkzeug's `None` sentinel for automatic derivation. Ensure the existing disabled-matching host cases remain covered. ## Fix Focus Areas - src/flask/app.py[438-445] - tests/test_basic.py[1750-1771] ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
